'''Jesper Møller''' (also written ''Moller'' or ''Moeller''; born December 6, 1957)<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://people.math.aau.dk/~jm/|title=Homepage for Jesper Møller|website=people.math.aau.dk|accessdate=4 December 2022}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Jesper Møller|url=https://vbn.aau.dk/en/persons/109843|access-date=2020-08-27|website=Aalborg University's Research Portal|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> is a Danish mathematician.

He is a professor at the Department of Mathematical Sciences, [[Aalborg University]], where he conducts research and teaching in [[mathematical statistics]] and [[probability theory]]. In 2012, he created the Bachelor and Master's Programmes in Mathematics and Technology at [[Aalborg University]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aalborg University – Knowledge for the World|url=https://www.en.aau.dk/|website=www.en.aau.dk}}</ref>

He was born in [[Nakskov]], [[Denmark]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://blaabog.dk/biography/?id=118765|title=Biografi|website=Kraks Blå Bog}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
Jesper Møller is [[Master of Science|M.Sc.]] ([[cand.scient.]]) in [[mathematics]] and [[mathematical statistics]] ([[Aarhus University]]), 1984; [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in [[mathematical statistics]] ([[Aarhus University]]), 1988; and [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc.]] ([[Doctor of Science|dr.scient.]]; title of dissertation: `Aspects of Spatial Statistics, Stochastic Geometry and Markov Chain Monte Carlo´; [[Aalborg University]]), 2000.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Jesper Møller – ScienceWatch.com|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/inter/aut/2008/08-jul/08julMoller/|access-date=2020-08-21|website=archive.sciencewatch.com}}</ref>

He was Assistant Professor and Associate Professor at [[Aarhus University]], 1988–1995, Associate Professor at Aalborg University, 1996–2000, and Professor at Aalborg University since 2001.

== Research ==
Jesper Møller's research interests<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> include
* [[spatial statistics]] (in particular [[statistical model]]s and methods for [[Point process|spatial point processes]]),
* [[stochastic geometry]] (in particular random t[[Tessellation|essellations]]),
* [[stochastic simulation]] ([[Markov chain Monte Carlo|Markov-chain Monte Carlo methods]] and [https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/statistics/staff/academic-research/thonnes/personal/perfect/ perfect simulation] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170613100720/http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/statistics/staff/academic-research/thonnes/personal/perfect |date=2017-06-13 }}).

His research has been supported by project grants from [https://dg.dk/en/ Danish National Research Foundation], [[Danish Council for Independent Research|Independent Research Fund Denmark]], [[European Union|EU]], [[Velux Foundation]], and [[Spar Nord]] Foundation. He has been Associated Editor of [[Annals of Applied Probability]], [[Advances in Applied Probability]], [[Bernoulli Society for Mathematical Statistics and Probability|Bernoulli]], and Associate Editor and National Editor of [[Scandinavian Journal of Statistics|the Scandinavian Journal of Statistics.]]

== Distinctions ==
* Elected Fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics, 1998.
* [[Spar Nord]] Foundation Research Price (DKK 250,000), 2000.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aau.dk/om-aau/historie-priser/aarsfest/ceremoni/prismodtagere-aarsfest/|title=Prismodtagere ved AAU's årsfest|website=www.aau.dk}}</ref>
* Presentation of a read-paper at a [[Royal Statistical Society]] Meeting in [[London]], 2005.
* Plenary Talk of 3 hours at the 21st Nordic Conference on [[Mathematical statistics|Mathematical Statistics]], presenting an invited paper for [[Scandinavian Journal of Statistics|the Scandinavian Journal of Statistics]].
* Rising Star in the field of Mathematics ([[Thomson Reuters]]), 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/inter/aut/2008/08-jul/08julMoller/|title=Jesper Møller – ScienceWatch.com|website=archive.sciencewatch.com}}</ref>
* [[Knight of the order of Dannebrog|Knight of the Order of Dannebrog]], 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://kongehuset.dk/modtagere-af-danske-dekorationer |title=Modtagere af danske dekorationer &#124; Kongehuset |access-date=2020-08-31 |archive-date=2019-05-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190512015518/http://kongehuset.dk/modtagere-af-danske-dekorationer |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Professorem Hospitem, [[Charles University]], [[Prague]], since 2020.

== Selected publications ==
Some of his publications are given as follows:<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Jesper Møller|url=https://vbn.aau.dk/en/persons/109843/publications/|access-date=2020-08-21|website=Aalborg University's Research Portal|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=9RBifrgAAAAJ&hl=da|title=Jesper Møller – Google Scholar|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

* J. Møller (1989). Random tessellations in R^d. ''Advances in Applied Probability'', 21:37–73.
* A. Baddeley and J. Møller (1989). Nearest-neighbour Markov point processes and random sets. ''International Statistical Review'', 2:89–121.
* J.L. Jensen and J. Møller (1991). Pseudolikelihood for exponential family models of spatial point processes. ''Annals of Applied Probability'', 3:445-461.
* J. Møller (1994). ''Lectures on Random Voronoi Tessellations.'' Lecture Notes in Statistics 87, Springer-Verlag, New York.
* C.J. Geyer and J. Møller (1994). Simulation procedures and likelihood inference for spatial point processes. ''Scandinavian Journal of Statistics'', 21:359–373.
* J. Møller, A.R. Syversveen and R.P. Waagepetersen (1998). Log Gaussian Cox processes. ''Scandinavian Journal of Statistics'', 25:451–482.
* W.S. Kendall and J. Møller (2000). Perfect simulation using dominating processes on ordered spaces, with application to locally stable point processes. ''Advances in Applied Probability'', 32:844–865.
* J. Møller (2003). Shot noise Cox processes. ''Advances in Applied Probability'', 35, 614–640.
* J. Møller and R.P. Waagepetersen (2004). ''Statistical Inference and Simulation for Spatial Point Processes''. Chapman and Hall/CRC, Boca Raton.
* A. Baddeley, R. Turner, J. Møller and M. Hazelton (2005). Residual analysis for spatial point processes (with discussion). ''Journal of Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Statistical Methodology)'', 67, 617–666.
* J. Møller, A.N. Pettitt, K.K. Berthelsen and R.W. Reeves (2006). An efficient Markov chain Monte Carlo method for distributions with intractable normalising constants. ''Biometrika'', 93, 451–458.
* J. Møller and R.P. Waagepetersen (2007). Modern statistics for spatial point processes (with discussion). ''Scandinavian Journal of Statistics'', 34, 643–711.
* A. Baddeley, E. Rubak and J. Møller (2011). Score, pseudo-score and residual diagnostics for goodness-of-fit of spatial point process models. ''Statistical Science'', 26, 613–646.
* F. Lavancier, J. Møller and E. Rubak (2015). Determinantal point process models and statistical inference. ''Journal of Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Statistical Methodology)'', 77, 853–877.
* E. Anderes, J. Møller and J.G. Rasmussen (2020). Isotropic covariance functions on graphs and their edges. To appear in ''Annals of Statistics''. Available at arXiv:1710.01295.
